title: Unexpected FX conversion despite sufficient balance
text: Recently, my experience with Revolut has been mostly negative, especially when it comes to how they handle complaints.In my case, a single card payment was later split into multiple transactions by the merchant (I purchased flight tickets). The original amount was released back in CZK, so there were sufficient funds available to cover all four transactions. However, although all transactions were in CZK, Revolut internally converted one transaction from CZK to EUR and charged it from my EUR balance, resulting in additional costs. Their explanation was inconsistent and did not reflect how the transaction was actually processed. They claim that one of the transactions was in EUR, but if that were the case, it would have been deducted directly from my EUR balance (which also had sufficient funds) without any conversion.In addition, a weekend exchange fee was applied even though the conversion took place on a weekday (Tuesday). This fee was later refunded, but this situation highlights how inconsistent and poorly designed their system is, raising questions about how these processes are implemented. It is also difficult to understand why this refund is presented as a "gesture of goodwill", rather than a correction of an apparent issue.Customer support was generally unhelpful and did not seem to understand the root cause of the issue. I was passed between multiple agents, but the responses felt repetitive and scripted, which made the experience frustrating and difficult to resolve.
